record.paper_title: Some open problems in low dimensional dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let p_n be the probability that the zero solution of an n-th order linear random differential equation with independent standard normal coefficients is globally asymptotically stable. Find the asymptotic expansion of p_n as n → ∞ and determine whether the sequence p_n is strictly decreasing.

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let pn be the probability that the zero solution of the n-th order linear random diﬀerential equation (18) is globally asymptotically stable. Find the asymptotic expansion of pn at n =∞. Is it true that the sequence pn is strictly decreasing?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer n ≥ 1, let a_0, a_1, ..., a_{n-1} be independent standard normal random variables, and consider the random n-th order linear homogeneous differential equation with constant coefficients

    y^(n)(t) + a_{n-1} y^(n-1)(t) + ... + a_1 y'(t) + a_0 y(t) = 0,

so that its characteristic polynomial is
    P_n(z) = z^n + a_{n-1} z^{n-1} + ... + a_1 z + a_0.

Let p_n denote the probability that the zero solution of this equation is globally asymptotically stable, equivalently the probability that every root of P_n(z) has strictly negative real part (i.e. P_n is a Hurwitz polynomial).

(a) Determine the full asymptotic expansion of p_n as n → ∞.
(b) Decide whether the sequence (p_n)_{n ≥ 1} is strictly decreasing.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem on the asymptotics and monotonicity of the probability that a random Hurwitz polynomial with i.i.d. standard normal coefficients is stable. Standard web searches did not find an explicit resolution of either the asymptotic expansion of p_n or the strict-monotonicity claim; related literature on random Hurwitz stability addresses bounds and special cases rather than a full asymptotic expansion, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Routh–Hurwitz stability criterion
status_evidence.snippet: A polynomial is Hurwitz (stable) iff all roots have negative real part; equivalent to asymptotic stability of the corresponding linear ODE.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard equivalence used in defining p_n, but no asymptotic formula for the Gaussian random case.

status_evidence.title: Robust Stability of Hurwitz Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs robustly stable Hurwitz polynomial families via orthogonal polynomial techniques.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature concerns deterministic/robust stability, not the probabilistic asymptotics of p_n.
